name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of D+22
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot
Heavy outside spending opposing Gilbert but markets still price him near-certain
model.rationale: The seat's D+22 partisan lean and Polymarket pricing near 96% for the Democrat point to a safe hold despite the open seat and substantial outside opposition spending. Gilbert's fundraising edge over Brown reinforces the expected outcome.
model.watch: The large outside spending against Gilbert is unusual for a safe seat; any credible polling showing a tighter race would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Frederica Wilson's retirement leaves this Miami-area district open, but its D+22 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic hands on paper. Democrat Oliver Gilbert has out-raised Republican Te Mayonna Brown and benefits from outside support, though outside groups have also spent heavily opposing him. No general-election polls are available, and no expert raters cover the race.

Prediction markets price the Democratic candidate at roughly 96%, consistent with a comfortable hold. The forecast expects a Democratic win by a wide, though slightly reduced, margin given the open-seat dynamics and opposition spending.
